'''Rafael''' "'''Rafa'''" '''Chaves Câmara''' ({{IPA|pt-BR|ʁafaˈɛw ˈkɐ̃mɐɾɐ|lang}}; born 5 May 2005) is a Brazilian [[racing driver]] who competes in Formula One for [[Haas F1 Team|Haas]] and the [[FIA Formula 2 Championship]] for [[Invicta Racing]] as part of the [[Ferrari Driver Academy]].

Born and raised in [[Pernambuco]], Câmara began competitive [[kart racing]] aged six, winning three [[List of international kart racing champions|international titles]] before graduating to [[junior formulae]] in 2022. He debuted in [[Formula 4]] with [[Prema Racing|Prema]], finishing runner-up to [[Charlie Wurz]] in the [[2022 Formula 4 UAE Championship|UAE Championship]] and third in both the [[2022 Italian F4 Championship|Italian]] and [[2022 ADAC Formula 4 Championship|ADAC]] Championships. He progressed to [[Formula Regional]] in 2023, where he claimed third in the [[2023 Formula Regional Middle East Championship|Middle East]] and multiple victories in the [[2023 Formula Regional European Championship|European Championship]], which he won the [[2024 Formula Regional European Championship|following season]] with Prema. Upon his graduation to [[FIA Formula 3]], he won the championship in [[2025 FIA Formula 3 Championship|his rookie season]] with [[Trident Motorsport|Trident]].

A member of the [[Ferrari Driver Academy]] since 2022, Câmara debuted in [[Formula One]] with [[Haas F1 Team|Haas]] at the [[2026 São Paulo Grand Prix]], prior to his full-time promotion in {{F1|2027}}. Câmara is contracted to remain at Haas until at least the end of the 2028 season.

== Early life and family background ==
Rafael Chaves Câmara was born on 5 May 2005 in [[Boa Viagem, Recife]], Pernambuco, Brazil.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Vasconcelos |first=Carlos |date=2025-08-04 |title=Piloto pernambucano, que começou no kart, é aposta na Ferrari e se credencia para F1 |url=https://www.publico.pt/2025/08/04/publico-brasil/noticia/piloto-pernambucano-comecou-kart-aposta-ferrari-credencia-f1-2142903 |access-date=2025-08-12 |website=PÚBLICO |language=pt}}</ref> His father, Amaro Câmara, is a [[lawyer]] while his mother, Paula Chaves, is a businesswoman.<ref>{{Cite web |last=JC |date=2025-08-05 |title=Campeão |url=https://jc.uol.com.br/social1/joao-alberto/2025/08/05/a-mudanca-do-nome-de-esporte-para-sport.html |access-date=2025-08-12 |website=JC |language=pt-br}}</ref> His maternal grandmother, Niége Rossiter, was a pioneer in Recife motorsports during the 1960s.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-08-08 |title=Campeão da F3, Rafael Câmara destaca avó que foi pilota em Recife |url=https://ge.globo.com/motor/noticia/2025/08/08/campeao-da-f3-rafael-camara-destaca-avo-que-foi-pilota-em-recife-pioneira.ghtml |access-date=2025-08-12 |website=ge |language=pt-br}}</ref>

== Junior racing career ==

=== Karting (2011–2021) ===
Câmara began karting in 2011, where he competed in the Pernambuco's State Championship. He would soon move into international competitions, after winning titles in all national and regional championships that he participated, garnering particular success in 2019 by finishing second in the [[Karting World Championship]], driving in the [[OKJ (karting)|OK Junior]] class for Forza Racing.<ref>{{Cite web |date=13 September 2019 |title=Rafael Câmara reaches for the stars in Finland |url=https://tkart.it/en/features/rafael-camara-reaches-for-the-stars-in-finland/ |access-date=30 December 2022 |website=TKART – News, tips, tech about karting |language=en-GB}}</ref> Having finished fifth in the [[CIK-FIA Karting European Championship|European Championship]] during his first year of senior karting, Câmara would close his karting career in 2021 by winning a number of series, such as the [[WSK Champions Cup]] and [[WSK Super Master Series]], as well as taking vice-champion status in the European Championship.<ref>{{Cite web |date=21 February 2021 |title=WSK CHAMPIONS CUP: DAS SIND DIE ERSTEN MEISTER DES JAHRES! |url=https://www.motorsport-xl.de/news/2021/WSK/WSK-Champions-Cup-Das-sind-die-ersten-Meister-des-Jahres-41190.html |website=motorsport-xl.de}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=The 2021 Champions of the WSK Super Master Series - automobilsport.com |url=https://www.automobilsport.com/race-categories--24,222331,The-2021-Champions-of-the-WSK-Super-Master-Series,news.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210618021926/https://www.automobilsport.com/race-categories--24,222331,The-2021-Champions-of-the-WSK-Super-Master-Series,news.htm |url-status=usurped |archive-date=June 18, 2021 |access-date=30 December 2022 |website=www.automobilsport.com}}</ref><ref>{{Citation |title=2021 European CHAMPIONS 🏆 (Kart Republic Official Report) |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wM3Lj0lOi88 |language=en |access-date=30 December 2022}}</ref>

=== Formula 4 (2022) ===
==== F4 UAE ====
In 2022, Câmara made his single-seater debut, competing in the [[2022 Formula 4 UAE Championship|F4 UAE Championship]] with [[Prema Racing]] to prepare for his main campaigns in Europe.<ref name="PremaSeason">{{Cite web |date=17 January 2022 |title=PREMA, Abu Dhabi Racing enter 2022 F4 UAE Season |url=https://premapowerteam.com/en/news.php?id_news=18867 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220117110713/https://premapowerteam.com/en/news.php?id_news=18867 |archive-date=17 January 2022 |website=[[Prema Powerteam]]}}</ref> Having missed the opening round due to contracting [[COVID-19]], Câmara scored his first podium at round two in [[Dubai Autodrome|Dubai]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Parker |first=Charlie |date=30 January 2022 |title=4 takeaways from F4 UAE Round 2: James Wharton dominates & Tatuus shows great racing |url=https://feederseries.net/2022/01/30/4-takeaways-from-f4-uae-round-2-james-wharton-dominates-tatuus-shows-great-racing/ |access-date=30 December 2022 |website=Feeder Series |language=en}}</ref> before achieving his first pair of car racing victories at the same venue the following weekend.<ref>{{Cite web |date=6 February 2022 |title=Red flag rules, Aiden Neate leads: 5 takeaways from F4 UAE Round 3 |url=https://feederseries.net/2022/02/06/red-flag-rules-aiden-neate-leads-5-takeaways-from-f4-uae-round-3/ |access-date=30 December 2022 |website=Feeder Series |language=en}}</ref> The penultimate event of the campaign brought even more success, as Câmara won three of the four races, putting himself in title contention before the season finale.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Parker |first=Charlie |date=13 February 2022 |title=Is the title Charlie Wurz's to lose? 4 takeaways from F4 UAE Round 4 at Dubai |url=https://feederseries.net/2022/02/13/is-the-title-charlie-wurzs-to-lose-4-takeaways-from-f4-uae-round-4-at-dubai/ |access-date=30 December 2022 |website=Feeder Series |language=en}}</ref> Despite winning Race 1 at [[Yas Marina Circuit|Yas Marina]], a collision in the third race forced his retirement from the race and clinched the title for teammate [[Charlie Wurz]]. Câmara ended up second in the standings and first in the rookie championship with 6 wins.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Parker |first=Charlie |date=21 February 2022 |title=Wurz holds off late Camara surge to win F4 UAE title: 4 takeaways from Round 5 |url=https://feederseries.net/2022/02/21/wurz-holds-off-late-cmara-surge-to-win-f4-uae-title-4-takeaways-from-round-5/ |access-date=30 December 2022 |website=Feeder Series |language=en}}</ref>

==== Italian F4 ====
[[File:F4 Italy 2022 Nr. 88 (2).jpg|thumb|right|Câmara racing in the [[2022 Italian F4 Championship]] at the [[Red Bull Ring]].]]
In tandem with his ADAC F4 campaign, Câmara also competed in [[2022 Italian F4 Championship|Italian F4]] with [[Prema Racing]]. He experienced a competitive start to his campaign, inheriting victory at the season opener in [[Imola Circuit|Imola]] when race leader Antonelli experienced a gearbox failure in the closing laps.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Studenkov |first=Alexander |date=10 May 2022 |title=The Alex Dunne Show: 4 takeaways from Italian F4 at Imola |url=https://feederseries.net/2022/05/10/the-alex-dunne-show-4-takeaways-from-italian-f4-at-imola/ |access-date=30 December 2022 |website=Feeder Series |language=en}}</ref> Another victory followed at [[Misano World Circuit Marco Simoncelli|Misano]], where the Brazilian proved his opportunism by overtaking his Italian teammate at the safety car restart,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Studenkov |first=Alexander |date=6 June 2022 |title=Antonelli bounces back in dominant display: 4 takeaways from Italian F4 at Misano |url=https://feederseries.net/2022/06/06/antonelli-bounces-back-in-dominant-display-4-takeaways-from-italian-f4-at-misano/ |access-date=30 December 2022 |website=Feeder Series |language=en}}</ref> which was then followed by another impressive weekend at [[Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps|Spa]], where, having stalled from pole position in Race 3, Câmara recovered to third by the checkered flag.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Studenkov |first=Alexander |date=21 June 2022 |title=Antonelli's masterclass and Câmara's comeback: 4 takeaways from Italian F4 at Spa |url=https://feederseries.net/2022/06/21/antonellis-masterclass-and-camaras-comeback-4-takeaways-from-italian-f4-at-spa/ |access-date=30 December 2022 |website=Feeder Series |language=en}}</ref> More podiums came at [[Vallelunga Circuit|Vallelunga]] and the [[Red Bull Ring]], before Câmara experienced his first and only podium-lacking event of the year at [[Monza Circuit|Monza]]. He finished his season third in the championship, falling behind [[Alex Dunne]] at the final round after a collision with the Irishman at the first corner.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Formula4 Italian Championship – Certified by FIA WSK Promotion Official Site- PREMA Racing, Antonelli take Italian Formula 4 Driver Championship with triple Mugello win |url=http://www.f4championship.com/news/673/PREMA%20Racing,%20Antonelli%20take%20Italian%20Formula%204%20Driver%20Championship%20with%20triple%20Mugello%20win |access-date=30 December 2022 |website=www.f4championship.com}}</ref>

=== Formula Regional (2023–2024) ===
==== 2023: Maiden victories ====
[[File:FREC 2023 Spielberg Nr. 8 (2) Câmara.jpg|thumb|left|Câmara racing in the [[2023 Formula Regional European Championship]] at the [[Red Bull Ring]].]]
During pre-season, Câmara did a full season in the [[2023 Formula Regional Middle East Championship]] with [[Mumbai Falcons]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Wood|first=Ida|date=9 January 2023|title=Prema reveals big name additions to FRMEC and F4 UAE line-ups|url=https://formulascout.com/prema-reveals-big-name-additions-to-frmec-and-f4-uae-line-ups/102685|access-date=9 January 2023|website=Formula Scout|language=en-GB}}</ref> Despite not winning a race, Câmara claimed six podiums that took him to third in the standings.<ref name="fguide">{{cite web|date=21 December 2023|last=Spadi|first=Daniele|title=Ferrari Driver Academy: 2023 driver-by-driver review|url=https://feederseries.net/2023/12/21/ferrari-driver-academy-2023-driver-by-driver-review/|website=Feeder Series|access-date=1 May 2025}}</ref>

Having tested with the team at the end of 2022, Câmara progressed to the [[2023 Formula Regional European Championship|Formula Regional European Championship]] with [[Prema Racing]] the following year, driving alongside F4 teammate Antonelli and category veteran [[Lorenzo Fluxá]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=TopCarNews |date=2022-12-16 |title=Rafael Câmara subirá a FRECA con PREMA Racing – TopCarNews |url=https://es.topcarnews.net/rafael-camara-subira-a-freca-con-prema-racing-v5313.html |access-date=2022-12-30 |website=topcarnews.net |language=es-es |archive-date=30 December 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221230123233/https://es.topcarnews.net/rafael-camara-subira-a-freca-con-prema-racing-v5313.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> He took his maiden win in the series during the first race at [[Spa-Francorchamps]].<ref>{{cite web|date=30 June 2023|last=Wood|first=Ida|title=Camara collects his first FREC win in Spa race one|url=https://formulascout.com/camara-collects-his-first-frec-win-in-spa-race-one/108593|website=Formula Scout|access-date=1 May 2025}}</ref> With a second win at [[Red Bull Ring]] and three additional podiums, Câmara finished fifth in the standings.<ref name="fguide" />

==== 2024: Record-breaking first junior championship ====
[[File:FREC 2024 Mogyoród Nr. 5 Camara.jpg|thumb|right|Câmara (pictured at the [[Hungaroring]]) claimed the [[2024 Formula Regional European Championship]] title, earning a record-breaking 7 wins.]]
Câmara remained with [[Prema Racing]] for the [[2024 Formula Regional European Championship|2024 FRECA season]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Wood|first=Ida|date=13 December 2023|title=Rafael Camara commits to second FREC season with Prema|url=https://formulascout.com/rafael-camara-commits-to-second-frec-season-with-prema/114045|access-date=14 December 2023|website=Formula Scout|language=en-GB}}</ref> He began the season with a fairly large lead, equalling his podiums from the previous season and claiming four wins in the first three rounds.<ref>{{cite web |last=Gascoigne |first=Roger |date=13 August 2024 |title=Can anyone catch Camara after FREC's summer break? |url=https://formulascout.com/can-anyone-catch-camara-after-frecs-summer-break/122495 |website=Formula Scout |access-date=3 June 2025}}</ref> Though going winless for the next two rounds, he cemented himself as a championship favourite with a win from pole at the first race at [[Circuit Paul Ricard|Paul Ricard]] and a lead of 50 points from second place, fellow [[Ferrari Driver Academy|Ferrari junior]] [[Tuukka Taponen]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Brusa |first=Francesca |date=9 August 2024 |title=FRECA mid-season review: Can resurgent Taponen dethrone Ferrari stablemate Câmara? |url=https://feederseries.net/2024/08/09/freca-mid-season-review-can-resurgent-taponen-dethrone-ferrari-stablemate-camara/ |website=Feeder Series |access-date=3 June 2025}}</ref> After the summer break, Câmara won another race at [[Imola Circuit|Imola]] before a pointless weekend at the [[Red Bull Ring]]. Despite the slight setback, he clinched the title in [[Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya|Barcelona]] with one round remaining after a podium and a fourth place. One final win at [[Monza Circuit|Monza]] resulted in a total of seven wins, the most wins in a single FRECA season. He scored points in every round except for one, never qualified outside the top-four and had a 75-point lead over second place, [[James Wharton (racing driver)|James Wharton]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Gascoigne |first=Roger |date=21 December 2024 |title=FREC season review: How Camara showed his class with dominant title |url=https://formulascout.com/frec-season-review-how-camara-showed-his-class-with-dominant-title/125747 |website=Formula Scout |access-date=3 June 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|date=31 December 2025|last=Brusa|first=Francesca|title=2024 Feeder Series Hall of Fame|url=https://feederseries.net/2024/12/31/2024-feeder-series-hall-of-fame/|website=Feeder Series|access-date=1 May 2025}}</ref>

Additionally, Câmara competed in the [[2024 Formula Regional Middle East Championship|2024 FRME season]], remaining with [[Mumbai Falcons]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wood |first=Ida |date=8 January 2024 |title=Prema reveals it and Mumbai Falcons' line-ups for FRME and F4 UAE |url=https://formulascout.com/prema-reveals-it-and-mumbai-falcons-line-ups-for-frme-and-f4-uae/114757 |access-date=17 October 2024 |website=Formula Scout |language=en-US}}</ref> He finished third in the championship with two wins.<ref>{{cite web|date=10 February 2024|last=Wood|first=Ida|title=Camara gets his second FRME win in safety car-filled race|url=https://formulascout.com/camara-gets-his-second-frme-win-in-safety-car-filled-race/115557|website=Formula Scout|access-date=1 May 2025}}</ref>

expecting to start the season' with three poles in a row |url=https://feederseries.net/2025/05/16/f3-points-leader-camara-was-not-expecting-to-start-the-season-with-three-poles-in-a-row/ pole position in [[2025 Barcelona Formula 3 round|Barcelona]], the first driver to accomplish this feat in the series and converted it successfully to his third feature race win having led every lap.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Spadi |first=Daniele |date=30 May 2025 |title=Câmara takes record fourth F3 pole in Barcelona as track position proves key Câmara clinched the championship at the penultimate round after finishing first in the feature race at the [[Hungaroring]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Vinel |first=Ben |date=4 August 2025 |title=New F3 champion Rafael Camara on path to emulate Charles Leclerc at Ferrari |url=https://www.motorsport.com/fia-f3/news/new-f3-champion-rafael-camara-on-path-to-emulate-charles-leclerc-at-ferrari/10748449/ |work=Motorsport Magazine |access-date=15 September 2025}}</ref> He was the first driver to do so since the inception of the championship in 2019.<ref>{{cite news |last=Suttill |first=Josh |date=3 August 2025 |title=Ferrari's new champion has moved out of Antonelli's shadow |url=https://www.the-race.com/formula-1/ferrari-f3-champion-rafael-camara-oscar-piastri-trajectory |work=The Race |access-date=4 August 2025}}</ref>
